segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. You can find a video version of this podcast to watch with subtitles

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and a free worksheet to help you learn at bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Georgie, how are you today?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm pretty good today, thank you Neil. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I am much better than I was this morning.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh, how were you feeling this morning?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I was really grumpy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh, why is that?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I'll tell you in a minute, but that's what we're talking about today, being grumpy, which means being in a bad mood.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So you said you were feeling grumpy this morning. I didn't notice that. Why were you feeling grumpy this morning?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I get really grumpy if I'm hungry or tired and very, very grumpy if I'm hungry and tired.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh no. Is that how you were feeling this morning then?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah. It's very hot at the moment. It's difficult to sleep.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we also didn't have any food in the fridge.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So I came to work hungry and tired. And so I was grumpy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh, well, you hid it very well. I didn't notice that.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I've felt cheerful all day so far.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, you're always cheerful, Georgie. Or are you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I no I not always cheerful Mostly I have to say mostly I am But there are certain times of the month that make me feel very grumpy And when I in a bad mood I become a bit irritable Small things that other people do annoy me And sometimes it not for any reason or it for a very small reason And I shouldn be so grumpy

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, Georgie, what kind of things make you grumpy?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, as I said, there are certain times of the month where I feel grumpy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But other things that make me grumpy, usually if it's a really sunny day outside and I'm stuck inside working,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: that makes me feel a bit grumpy because I would prefer to be outside in the sun, in the park, spending time in the fresh air.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But instead, I'm working.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So you said that you're grumpy when you're hungry or tired.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What kind of things do you do to cheer yourself up?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, yeah, to cheer myself up, to feel better.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, eat something and sleep.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I guess also do something relaxing.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Maybe do some exercise.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Exercise is a really good thing to lift your mood.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes I as I said like to be outside That will make me that will put me in a better mood going for a walk in the park being in nature with some fresh air I also really like to put some upbeat music on and dance around my bedroom

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I like doing that.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: That cheers me up.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think that would cheer everybody up.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What if they got to watch it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What do you think about people who are always grumpy?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I do know someone who's always grumpy, but he's so grumpy it's almost funny.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Like he knows he's grumpy and people make little jokes about it and he kind of knows he's grumpy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So it's entertaining for you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, but it's still not really that nice to be close to.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, a bit of a negative energy.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Absolutely.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Absolutely. Georgie, are you good at hiding it when you are grumpy?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, apparently I am because I sometimes am grumpy and you said that I never seem grumpy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So maybe I am very good at hiding it.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think it's good not to let other people feel your negativity coming out of you.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But on the other hand, I think it's also good to share how you feel sometimes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Okay, so perhaps you are really grumpy right now, even though you seem cheerful.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Even though I have a big smile on my face, yeah.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It because I had a coffee I feeling good

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK Georgie it time now to recap the language that we used in this podcast

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, we had grumpy, which means easily annoyed, negative or in a bad mood.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, in a bad mood.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And the opposite of that is in a good mood when you're feeling happy and cheerful.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Cheerful is another word we heard today.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, cheerful is another word for happy, but you show it in an obvious way, maybe by smiling.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yep, and we've got the phrasal verb cheer up, which means to become happy or cheerful.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, for example, I cheer myself up by dancing alone in my bedroom.
